verses.1: A Psalm by Asaph: Truly, God is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are upright.
verses.2: But as for me, my feet nearly slipped, my steps had nearly gone astray.
verses.3: For I envied the arrogant, seeing the peace of the wicked.
verses.4: For there is no anguish in their death, and their body is sound and at ease.
verses.5: They are not in trouble like others, nor are they punished like the rest of humanity.
verses.6: Therefore, their pride surrounds them, and they wrap themselves in iniquity and wrong.
verses.7: Their eyes glisten with fatness, their hearts overflow with thoughts.
verses.8: They scoff and speak evil; they threaten from on high.
verses.9: Their mouths are set like the heavens, and their tongues roam the earth.
verses.10: Therefore, their people return to confusion, and their days are filled with abundance for them.
verses.11: And they say, How can God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?
verses.12: Behold, these are the wicked, yet they live in peace, having gained power.
verses.13: I have indeed declared my innocence in vain, washed my hands in innocence.
verses.14: I have been afflicted all day long, and your correction has come at dawn.
verses.15: If I had said, I will speak thus, I would have betrayed your children.
verses.16: I thought to understand this, but it was a burden to me.
verses.17: Until I entered the sanctuary of God, I came to understand their end.
verses.18: Indeed, you have set them on slippery ground; you have cast them down to ruin.
verses.19: How suddenly were they destroyed! They vanished as a dream when one awakens.
verses.20: Like a dream when one awakens, O Lord, when you look upon them, their image vanishes.
verses.21: For my heart was stirred with envy, my inner being was shaken.
verses.22: I have become brutish and did not understand; I was like a beast with you.
verses.23: Yet I am always with you, you have taken my right hand.
verses.24: You will guide me with your counsel and afterward receive me with glory.
verses.25: What do I have in heaven besides you? And apart from you, I desire nothing on earth.
verses.26: My flesh and heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
verses.27: For surely, those who are far from you will perish; you have destroyed all who are unfaithful to you.
verses.28: But as for me, it is good to be near God. I have made the Lord my refuge; I will tell of all your works in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "Behold, these are the wicked..." — the Hebrew uses the plural form רְשָׁעִים ("wicked") and שַׁלְוֵי עוֹלָם ("at peace forever"), which are rendered directly.
- v. 17: "Until I entered the sanctuary of God" — the phrase מִקְדְּשֵׁי־אֵל is plural, but the singular is used here for poetic clarity.
- v. 25: "What do I have in heaven besides you?" — the Hebrew uses מִי־לִי בַשָּׁמָיִם ("what is with me in heaven?"), which is translated idiomatically to retain natural English flow.
